target_customer: Web3 engineering teams building applications that need fast, reliable access to indexed on-chain data
problem: Blockchains act as the database for web3 apps, but querying and indexing their data is slow and painful, which blocked developers from building responsive products.
business_model: Usage-based developer API for hosted blockchain indexing and subgraphs
product_category: Web3 developer tools, blockchain data indexing

founders.name: Jonathan Kau
founders.background_notes: The YC page says the founding team were early employees at Airtable, Heap and Y Combinator, without assigning each employer to a person.

founders.name: Dan Li
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by YC and press coverage; individual employers not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ran multi-chain indexing on top of open source technology from The Graph, so the hard parts were reliability, speed and multi-chain infrastructure rather than inventing new indexing research.

defensibility.rationale: Built on open source Graph tooling with several hosted indexers and node providers able to offer the same service, so switching costs were low.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Alchemy acquired Satsuma in September 2023 and folded it into Alchemy Subgraphs, which Alchemy later discontinued on December 8, 2025 with users pointed to Goldsky.

market_need_then: Web3 application development was booming in 2021 and developers needed ways to query on-chain data. The founders cited indexing friction as a blocker, though dated third party demand evidence was not collected.

branding.domain_note: Used satsuma.xyz, a crypto-flavored TLD, not satsuma.com.

rebrands.why: Product merged into Alchemy's suite after the acquisition; Alchemy docs say formerly Satsuma.

brand_strength.rationale: Named customers such as Decentraland, Aragon and Syndicate and a short fruit name, but no sources show brand press, merch or community, and the name was retired within months of the acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Satsuma, started by early employees of Airtable, Heap and Y Combinator, built a hosted subgraph indexer for web3 developers and raised a $5 million seed in April 2023 led by Initialized Capital and Archetype. Five months later Alchemy acquired it for undisclosed terms and rebranded it Alchemy Subgraphs, which Alchemy shut down in December 2025. The soft landing label is an inference from the short independent life and later product shutdown.
